level: actual React product panels with isolated JSDOM and synthetic APIs
observed: Older success or failure cannot overwrite a later refresh; action completion causes a later refresh and retiring the instance prevents stale refresh.
When the latest snapshot fails, the old view stays visible with actionable controls disabled until a newer snapshot succeeds.
When dispatch rejects or its response is lost, in-flight pre-action reads cannot unlock stale controls; no automatic replay occurs.
A changed API or remounted component does not retain the previous host writable view; the generated product bundle was rebuilt and byte check passed.
limitations: The JSDOM tests exercise the actual React panel component and synthetic API promises, not a live browser, real machine pairing or complete product acceptance.
A successful fresh snapshot restores controls, but Host authorization remains authoritative and this UI is not an OS isolation or receipt proof boundary.
This change does not by itself prevent unsafe retries in the Host journal; separate backend work is in progress.
The remote tests verified these three UI source/test files and reused existing isolated fixture dependencies; no clean installation or full remote product deployment is claimed.
